idea: Heston and Sadka (2008) seasonality-adjusted 60-day forecast, with its exposure to the submitted 20-day forecast removed so the alpha carries only the information the submitted one lacks.
rationale_data: mid_term_seasonal_adjusted_return_forecast_60d and short_term_return_pred_r20_q1 (multi factor market return predictions, model category).
rationale_operators: vector_neut(): makes the 60-day forecast rank orthogonal to the 20-day forecast rank each day; rank() normalises both.

idea: Image-based 50-day return forecast (Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023), orthogonalised to the submitted 20-day forecast so the two do not trade alike.
rationale_data: predicted_stock_return_50d_image (option chart image return prediction) and short_term_return_pred_r20_q1 (multi factor market return predictions), both model category.
rationale_operators: vector_neut(): removes the cross-sectional exposure to the 20-day forecast; rank() normalises.

idea: Term structure of expected returns: Da and Warachka (2011) show the gap between long- and short-horizon forecasts carries information; here the 120-day minus the 20-day model forecast.
rationale_data: long_term_120d_regression_prediction and short_term_20d_regression_prediction (multi factor market return predictions, model category).
rationale_operators: the difference isolates the horizon disagreement; rank() normalises it.

idea: The part of the 120-day forecast that the 20-day forecast does not explain over the last quarter: slow information that short-horizon models miss (BRAIN Option6 guide prefers regression residuals to correlations).
rationale_data: long_term_120d_regression_prediction and short_term_20d_regression_prediction (multi factor market return predictions, model category).
rationale_operators: ts_regression(rettype=0): the residual of a 63-day time-series regression; rank() normalises.

idea: Fundamental law of active management (Grinold and Kahn): two weakly correlated forecasts (daily PnL correlation 0.18) of different horizons add breadth.
rationale_data: event_embedding_5d_regression_prediction and long_term_120d_regression_prediction (multi factor market return predictions, model category).
rationale_operators: rank() puts both forecasts on the same scale before adding them.

idea: Two chart-image CNN models (Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023) built on different networks; averaging their forecasts reduces model noise.
rationale_data: img30d_return_bisection_prob1_zackbatch and img30d_return_quintile (deep learning chart-based alpha, model category).
rationale_operators: rank() normalises each model's output before combining.

idea: Short- versus long-horizon chart signals: the 30-day minus the 60-day CNN probability captures whether the chart pattern points to a near-term move (Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023).
rationale_data: img30d_return_bisection_prob1_zackbatch and img60d_return_bisection_prob1_zackbatch (deep learning chart-based alpha, model category).
rationale_operators: the difference isolates the horizon gap; rank() normalises.

idea: Where a vendor alpha score stands relative to its own recent history: improvements in a stock's forecast, net of stable level differences.
rationale_data: alpha_score (AI equity alpha forecasts, model category), a vector field aggregated per stock.
rationale_operators: vec_avg(): one value per stock and day; ts_zscore(63): today versus the last quarter; rank() normalises.

idea: Revisions of a forecast: the one-month change in the seasonality-adjusted 60-day forecast (forecast revisions carry information, Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996).
rationale_data: mid_term_seasonal_adjusted_return_forecast_60d (multi factor market return predictions, model category).
rationale_operators: ts_delta(21): one-month change; rank() normalises.

idea: Agreement of two independent sources: option-implied and analyst-based forecasts; stocks favoured by both get the largest weight (Stambaugh, Yu and Yuan 2012 on conditioning).
rationale_data: option_quantile5_20d_pred and analyst_quantile1_120d_pred (multi-source market return prediction, model category).
rationale_operators: the product of the two ranks emphasises stocks high on both.

idea: Call-put implied volatility spread (Cremers and Weinbaum 2010; Bali and Hovakimian 2009), measured as each side's deviation from its own quarter so mechanical level differences cancel (BRAIN Option6 guide).
rationale_data: at-the-money call and put implied volatilities (option chart model, model category).
rationale_operators: ts_zscore(63): each volatility relative to its last quarter; the difference is the standardized spread; rank() normalises.

idea: The part of call implied volatility that put implied volatility does not explain over the last quarter: one-sided demand for calls signals informed bullish trading (Pan and Poteshman 2006; Cremers and Weinbaum 2010).
rationale_data: at-the-money call and put implied volatilities (option chart model, model category).
rationale_operators: ts_regression(rettype=0): residual of call IV on put IV over 63 days; rank() normalises.

idea: Implied-volatility skew relative to its own history: shifts in the smirk carry the information (Xing, Zhang and Zhao 2010); the plain level only reached Sharpe 0.74.
rationale_data: mean_volatility_skew_30d_short_term_2 (option horizon decomposition, model category).
rationale_operators: ts_zscore(63): today's skew versus the last quarter; rank() normalises.

idea: An, Ang, Bali and Cakici (2014): stocks whose call implied volatility rose over the past month outperform and those whose put implied volatility rose underperform.
rationale_data: 30-day at-the-money call and put implied volatilities (option horizon decomposition, model category).
rationale_operators: ts_delta(21): one-month changes; their difference is long call-volatility increases and short put-volatility increases; rank() normalises.

idea: The call-put spread (Cremers and Weinbaum 2010) compared within size deciles, so the bet does not lean on small stocks (BRAIN group-data guide; sub-universe robustness).
rationale_data: at-the-money call and put implied volatilities (option chart model) and market_capitalization_value_2 (scorings data) for the size groups, all model category.
rationale_operators: bucket(rank(size)) makes ten size groups, densify() removes empty ones, group_neutralize() demeans the ranked spread within each.

expression: s = rank(option_quantile5_20d_pred); w = rank(market_capitalization_value_2); ts_decay_linear(s, 3) * w + ts_decay_linear(s, 6) * (1 - w)
idea: Option-implied 20-day forecast (An et al. 2014 on option information), decayed faster in liquid names and slower in illiquid ones, BRAIN's suggested fix for a sub-universe near-miss.
rationale_data: option_quantile5_20d_pred (multi-source market return prediction) and market_capitalization_value_2 (scorings data), model category.
rationale_operators: ts_decay_linear(3) for large companies and (6) for small ones, blended by the rank of company size.

idea: Earnings forecast revisions (Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996): the consensus EPS estimate relative to its own last quarter captures recent revisions without per-share scale problems.
rationale_data: earnings_per_share_average (analyst estimate data for equity, analyst category): mean of the EPS estimates.
rationale_operators: ts_zscore(63): today versus the last quarter; rank() normalises across stocks.

idea: Revisions matter most when fresh (Hawkins, Chamberlin and Daniel 1984; BRAIN research-paper guide): trade the one-month relative EPS revision only in the days after the consensus changes, then hold.
rationale_data: earnings_per_share_average (analyst estimate data for equity, analyst category).
rationale_operators: days_from_last_change() <= 3 marks a fresh update; ts_delta/abs(ts_delay) is the relative revision; trade_when() holds positions between updates.

idea: Expected profitability trends: firms whose predicted profitability keeps improving outperform (Hou, Xue and Zhang 2015 profitability factor; Novy-Marx 2015 fundamental momentum).
rationale_data: anl82_netq_deltaprofitability_profitability2 (analyst estimate prediction data, analyst category).
rationale_operators: ts_regression on ts_step(1) over 63 days returns the slope (rettype=2); rank() normalises.

idea: Price-target revisions carry information beyond recommendations (Brav and Lehavy 2003): the bias-adjusted target relative to its own last quarter.
rationale_data: avg_first_biasfree_price_target_estimate (bias adjusted analyst forecasts, analyst category).
rationale_operators: ts_zscore(63): target versus its recent history; rank() normalises.

idea: Revision breadth: the share of analysts raising versus cutting their price targets (Brav and Lehavy 2003; breadth refinements of revision signals).
rationale_data: counts of upward and downward bias-free price target revisions and the number of targets (bias adjusted analyst forecasts, analyst category).
rationale_operators: the difference over the count (+1 to avoid dividing by zero) is net breadth; rank() normalises.

idea: Changes in expected profitability (Hou, Xue and Zhang 2015): the predicted quarterly profitability change relative to its own last quarter.
rationale_data: anl82_netq_deltaprofitability_profitability2 (analyst estimate prediction data, analyst category).
rationale_operators: ts_zscore(63): today versus the last quarter; rank() normalises.

idea: Three-month consensus EPS revision (Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 'REV6'): stocks with upward revisions keep outperforming.
rationale_data: eps_y1_estimate_change_3mo (global analyst factor signals, analyst category).
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the revision across stocks; industry neutralization compares within industries.

idea: Post-earnings-announcement drift (Bernard and Thomas 1989): take the position when a new earnings surprise is reported and hold it until the next one.
rationale_data: act_q_eps_surprisemean (broker estimates, analyst category): mean EPS surprise of the latest quarter.
rationale_operators: days_from_last_change() == 0 marks the report day; trade_when() enters then and holds; rank() normalises.

idea: Estimate-level revisions: each new broker estimate compared with that broker's previous one; the relative revision predicts returns (Givoly and Lakonishok 1979).
rationale_data: anl44_2_epsr_value and anl44_2_epsr_prevalue (integrated broker estimates, analyst category): current and previous estimate at each revision event.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the day's revisions; the difference over the previous value is the relative revision; ts_backfill(21) carries it between events; rank() normalises.

idea: Diether, Malloy and Scherbina (2002): high dispersion of analyst forecasts predicts lower returns.
rationale_data: anl44_best_eps_stddev and anl44_best_eps (integrated broker estimates, analyst category): dispersion and level of the EPS consensus.
rationale_operators: the standard deviation over the absolute consensus is the coefficient of variation; rank() and the minus sign short high disagreement.

idea: News tone predicts returns (Tetlock 2007; Tetlock, Saar-Tsechansky and Macskassy 2008): update the story sentiment signal on news days and hold it in between.
rationale_data: nws18_ssc (Ravenpack news data, news category): granular story sentiment from -1 to +1.
rationale_operators: vec_count() > 0 marks news days; vec_avg() averages the day's stories; trade_when() holds the position between news days.

idea: Headline sentiment from a deep network (Ke, Kelly and Xiu 2019 on text-based return prediction): update on days with headlines, hold otherwise.
rationale_data: mws82_sentiment (sentiment analysis from DNN, news category): per-headline sentiment.
rationale_operators: vec_count() > 0 marks headline days; vec_avg() averages them; trade_when() holds positions between them.

idea: Projected market impact of news flashes: prices take days to absorb news, so a forecast of the impact predicts the drift (Tetlock 2007; Ke, Kelly and Xiu 2019).
rationale_data: news_impact_projection_score (Ravenpack news data, news category).
rationale_operators: vec_count() > 0 marks news days; vec_avg() averages the day's scores; trade_when() holds positions in between.

idea: Tetlock (2011): investors react to novel news while stale news reverses, so tone matters most when the news is new; tone sets the side, novelty the size.
rationale_data: mean_composite_sentiment_score and mean_event_novelty_score (Ravenpack news data, news category).
rationale_operators: rank() - 0.5 centres the tone; multiplying by the rank of novelty scales positions by how new the news is.

idea: Fang and Peress (2009): stocks with little media coverage earn higher returns than heavily covered ones.
rationale_data: nws18_relevance (Ravenpack news data, news category): one entry per story, so its count measures coverage.
rationale_operators: vec_count() counts stories per day; ts_mean(63) averages coverage over a quarter; the minus sign buys neglected stocks.

idea: News momentum (Wang, Zhang and Zhu 2018): recent story tone, carried over short news gaps and smoothed over a week.
rationale_data: nws18_ssc (Ravenpack news data, news category).
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates stories; ts_backfill(5) bridges days without news; ts_decay_linear(5) weights recent days more; rank() normalises.

idea: Shorting demand shifts (Cohen, Diether and Malloy 2007): a rise in lending utilisation times fee relative to its own history predicts lower returns.
rationale_data: shrt7_combo_utilisation_x_rate (short selling model, model category).
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates; ts_zscore(63) compares with the last quarter; the minus sign shorts rising shorting pressure.

idea: Increases in the share of lendable shares on loan signal informed short selling (Cohen, Diether and Malloy 2007; Boehmer, Jones and Zhang 2008).
rationale_data: shrt7_combo_utilisation (short selling model, model category): normalised lending utilisation.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates; ts_delta(21) is the one-month change; the minus sign shorts rising utilisation.
